title: Praxis School Psychologist (5403) — 200 Source Questions + 100 Independent Practice Questions + 200 Guided Review
description: Contains 200 original source questions, 100 assistant-authored independent practice questions, and 200 source-derived guided-review activities. The assistant audit found 200 distinct independent content kernels. Two independently authored 100-question diagnostic batches linked to a 12-chapter learning library, targeted skill practice, and an optional 125-question timed simulation. The official 5403 test currently has 125 selected-response questions in 125 minutes; AlloFlow practice is not an official form or score.
contentReview: Assistant audit completed: 300 independent-practice items contain 200 distinct content kernels and 100 parallel variants under the normalized test. 200 additional activities are guided reasoning transformations, not independent exam questions. The 500-distinct-question target is not met.
disclaimer: Independent preparation material. Not affiliated with or endorsed by ETS or NASP. The official Praxis School Psychologist (5403) test currently has 125 selected-response questions in 125 minutes; the 100-item diagnostic batches are not official-length forms. Practice results are not official or scaled Praxis scores, pass predictions, credentials, psychological evaluations, diagnoses, mental-health treatment, legal advice, or substitutes for current federal, state, local, district, credential, ethical, crisis, consent, and mandated-reporting requirements.

items.prompt: Family representatives, paraprofessionals, and students attend an intervention committee, but meeting records show that their suggestions never alter the plans proposed by administrators. Which consultation redesign best addresses the power imbalance?

Share accessible evidence before deliberation, identify decisions participants can influence, use transparent facilitation criteria, and record the response to their input.
Rotate the meeting chair among professional staff while retaining the same proposal sequence, technical materials, and undocumented decision process.
Invite additional representatives to observe the meeting so the attendance list becomes more diverse without changing when or how decisions are made.

Begin separate decoding, visual-motor, and endurance interventions at the same time and use any overall improvement as confirmation that the combined explanation was correct.
Define a shared outcome, state competing alterable hypotheses, coordinate aligned observations and probes, and run a bounded trial that can distinguish among explanations.
Administer a broad individual battery before the team defines the performance pattern because standardized scores can select the correct disciplinary explanation.

items.prompt: A teacher now waits for the school psychologist to select every classroom adjustment and interpret each weekly graph. Which consultation step best develops the teacher's independent problem-solving capacity?

Stop attending immediately and ask the teacher to use prior recommendations independently, then evaluate capacity from the next report submitted.
Transfer graph interpretation to an administrator so the classroom teacher can focus on implementation rather than learning the decision process.

items.prompt: A psychologist believes lengthy assignments trigger escape behavior and notices several episodes that fit the hypothesis, but has not reviewed long assignments completed without disruption. What should happen next?

Collect additional examples when disruption follows a lengthy assignment because a larger set of confirming episodes will eventually establish the preferred hypothesis.
Ask the teacher whether the original explanation feels accurate and treat agreement between professionals as sufficient confirmation of the behavioral function.
Shorten every assignment at once and interpret any subsequent reduction as proof that length was causal without tracking other changes or untreated comparison conditions over time.
items.rationale: Confirmation bias is reduced by actively seeking exceptions, comparison conditions, and evidence that could refute a favored account. items.prompt: The psychologist who coordinated a classroom plan is leaving midyear, and a new provider will assume consultation duties. Which handoff best protects continuity without unnecessary disclosure?
choices: Give the incoming provider the psychologist's complete email archive and informal notes so no contextual detail is lost, then allow the provider to decide later what was relevant.
Transfer an authorized summary of the concern, current plan, roles, fidelity and outcome data, pending decisions, and next review; then reorient participants.
End the existing plan on the departure date and have the new provider restart problem identification so the consultation is entirely independent.
Leave a verbal summary with one administrator and ask that person to brief the new provider when scheduling permits, without confirming the next data review.

choiceRationales: Not the best answer. Bulk transfer can disclose unnecessary information and makes it harder to distinguish the current authorized plan from informal or obsolete discussion. A good handoff preserves the problem definition, active plan, responsibilities, implementation and outcome evidence, and next decision while limiting information to what is authorized and useful. items.prompt: A teacher says consultation no longer feels reliable because the psychologist missed a promised observation summary and did not provide an update. What response best begins repairing the working relationship?

Send a general intervention resource without discussing the missed commitment so renewed technical assistance can replace an uncomfortable relational conversation.
Acknowledge the missed commitment, apologize without defensiveness, ask its impact, agree on a realistic repair plan, and complete the follow-up.
Ask the teacher to send repeated reminders before future deadlines because shared responsibility means the consultee should prevent another missed follow-up.

Avoid showing any data and ask staff to brainstorm general behavior strategies without identifying the pattern the meeting is meant to address.

items.prompt: A seventh-grade science intervention has been delivered as planned for six weeks, but the student still cannot explain cause-and-effect relationships in unfamiliar experiments. What is the best next step for the school psychologist and teacher?

Continue the same lessons with added coaching and weekly fidelity observations, compare curriculum-based scores with the existing goal line, and delay changing the reasoning model until another full grading period is complete.
Replace science instruction with general study-skills counseling and use improved attendance as evidence that scientific reasoning has increased.
Recommend a disability category from the six-week trend because a flat intervention slope establishes the cause of the student's performance.

Allow an efficient response mode that reduces handwriting demand, keep spelling as the scored target, and document whether the access change alters interpretation.
Score handwriting speed and spelling accuracy as one combined outcome so the team can avoid distinguishing between the two skills.
Excuse the student from every spelling task and infer mastery from the quality of oral classroom participation.

Reduce the course goal to computation fluency because difficulty transferring a learned strategy shows that conceptual application should no longer be expected.

items.prompt: A student with decoding difficulty is trialing text-to-speech during social studies. The class goal is to evaluate understanding of historical arguments rather than oral reading. Which evaluation of the trial is most useful?

Reject the tool because listening support inevitably changes a content-knowledge task into a different and less rigorous curriculum.
Measure primarily how many minutes the student uses the software and disregard comprehension or the amount of adult assistance required.

choiceRationales: Correct. Assistive technology decisions should be based on the task, the access barrier, and evidence from realistic use. A structured trial should preserve the content construct and examine outcomes, usability, independence, burden, and student perspective before the team decides how the support should be used.

items.prompt: A multilingual middle school student can organize an argument during a conference but loses the structure when writing independently in English. Which intervention plan best uses the available evidence?

items.prompt: An eighth-grade student has visited the nurse repeatedly with headaches before oral presentations, yet medical information available to the school is inconclusive. What is the best school psychologist response?

Begin a clinical treatment protocol based solely on the nurse-visit pattern without discussing scope, consent, or other qualified supports.

Cancel all targeted groups because variation in nominations means schools cannot use any judgment when identifying students who may benefit.

items.prompt: During a class presentation, a student begins trembling, breathing rapidly, and saying, “I cannot do this.” There is no known plan on file. What should the school psychologist do first?

Escort the student to a quiet office, coach paced breathing until visible symptoms decrease, and arrange another presentation later that day because the episode appears limited to performance stress.

Send the student alone to an unsupervised hallway and wait until the next school day to determine whether support is needed.
items.rationale: Acute distress calls for calm, private, supervised stabilization and a brief check for immediate safety or health concerns. choiceRationales: Correct. Acute distress calls for calm, private, supervised stabilization and a brief check for immediate safety or health concerns. items.prompt: A recently transferred sixth-grade student eats alone, has stopped attending an extracurricular activity, and says school feels unfamiliar. No immediate safety concern is disclosed. Which response best builds protective support?

Ask about the student’s interests and preferred supports, connect the student with a trusted adult and compatible peer opportunity, address access barriers, and monitor adjustment.
Invite the student to a well-established peer club, assign a trained peer ambassador, and use attendance and club participation for six weeks before asking whether the match supports belonging.
Wait until the student fails a course because adjustment concerns should not receive school support unless they produce severe academic consequences.

items.prompt: After a private check finds no immediate safety concern, a student who has missed many assignments says, “Nothing I try matters.” Which brief school-based conversation best supports movement toward an achievable academic action?

Assure the student that the problem will disappear soon without selecting an action, support, or way to evaluate whether circumstances improve.
Ask about an exception when work was started, identify what made it possible, define one student-chosen next step, and agree on how progress will be noticed.
Complete the first missing assignment for the student so the grade improves before discussing ownership or an independent routine.

items.prompt: A six-week coping-skills group shows modest average improvement, but multilingual participants attended less often and report that examples did not fit their experiences. What is the strongest program response?

Exclude multilingual students from future groups so attendance rates and average outcomes are easier to interpret across participants.
Translate the session titles and declare the program culturally responsive without reviewing examples, participation conditions, or student feedback.
Disaggregate outcomes and participation, ask participants about barriers and relevance, examine fidelity and adaptations, revise access and content, and evaluate the next cycle.

items.prompt: A student posts a drawing in a shared class document showing a named classmate being harmed, then tells a peer it was “only a joke.” What should the school psychologist do?

Save the drawing, meet privately with the student to clarify intent and context, document a denial of weapon access and an agreement that the image was humorous, and close the concern in counseling notes before notifying the multidisciplinary safety team.
Announce to the class that the student is dangerous so classmates can report any other unusual behavior they have observed.
Conduct an extended interrogation alone and promise that the information will remain confidential regardless of what the student reveals.
items.rationale: A targeted depiction and named person require prompt preservation, consultation, and use of the school’s current multidisciplinary threat-assessment pathway. The response should be proportionate to evidence, protect potentially affected students, avoid public or diagnostic labels, and escalate immediately when the assessment identifies urgent danger.
choiceRationales: Correct. A targeted depiction and named person require prompt preservation, consultation, and use of the school’s current multidisciplinary threat-assessment pathway. The response should be proportionate to evidence, protect potentially affected students, avoid public or diagnostic labels, and escalate immediately when the assessment identifies urgent danger.

Not the best answer. A private interview and preservation are useful, but denial of access and stated humor do not justify solo closure or delaying the designated team’s contextual safety assessment. items.prompt: A middle school student tells the psychologist, “My friend keeps saying everyone would be better off if they did not wake up, but they made me promise not to tell.” What is the best response?

Thank the student for reporting, locate the friend promptly, activate the school safety pathway for a private risk assessment, and share information only with personnel needed for protection.
Ask the reporting student to monitor the friend overnight and return with proof before the school begins any assessment process.
Send a general wellness email to the entire grade and wait to see whether the friend independently requests an appointment.
items.rationale: Indirect reports of possible self-harm language should be taken seriously without assuming a conclusion. The psychologist should respond promptly through current school procedures, ensure the identified student is located and assessed by qualified personnel, protect the reporting student from carrying the safety burden, and document follow-up.

Additional detail may inform follow-up, but asking a peer to recruit or monitor the friend and waiting until dismissal delays direct location and trained assessment of a potentially urgent concern. items.prompt: During dismissal, an elementary student overturns furniture and throws classroom objects while other students are nearby. Which sequence is the most appropriate immediate school response?

Have trained crisis staff move the student to a designated low-stimulation room using the school’s standard physical escort whenever furniture is thrown, and evaluate afterward whether the level of danger required restrictive contact.
Move peers out of the area, summon trained assistance, use the least restrictive approved safety procedures, maintain observation, and conduct problem analysis only after stabilization.
Leave the student alone in the classroom and close the door so staff do not inadvertently reinforce the escalation with attention.

items.prompt: Observation shows that a student leaves cooperative-learning groups after peers repeatedly mock reading errors, and staff then permit solitary work. Which behavior plan best addresses the pattern?

Remove the student from cooperative work permanently because solitary completion appears to eliminate the leaving behavior.
Reward classmates whenever the student finishes alone because peer reinforcement is unrelated to the function of the student’s behavior.
Stop and monitor peer mistreatment, adjust the group context, teach an efficient help or pause request, reinforce safe participation, and measure both student and environmental outcomes.

items.prompt: A counseling-group member discovers that another student posted a screenshot of a private group comment in a peer chat. What should the school psychologist leading the group do first?

items.prompt: A fifth-grade team introduced a break-request card after an FBA indicated that difficult independent tasks often precede shouting. Staff respond quickly to shouting but frequently overlook the card. What should the school psychologist recommend first?

Require unprompted card use before honoring requests, then thin access after the first successful day so adults do not create dependence on the replacement response.

items.prompt: A student returns to school after emergency psychiatric care, and staff ask the school psychologist to obtain every treatment detail before allowing attendance. Which reentry approach is most appropriate?

Discontinue the intervention and adopt a program that promises shorter sessions, using the same assembly-prone schedule so the team can compare which curriculum produces faster improvement under ordinary conditions.
Continue the current schedule unchanged and extend every student’s participation until scores eventually improve.

Document coverage gaps, provide accessible administration routes, examine subgroup response patterns, and limit comparisons until participation better represents the intended population.

Abandon universal screening permanently because no school can obtain responses from every enrolled student.

Remove numerical and operational criteria so each team can rely on professional judgment without being constrained by district expectations.

items.prompt: Winter screening places 46% of one grade below benchmark while other grades range from 11% to 14%. What should the psychologist recommend before treating the pattern as twelve individual intervention needs?
choices: Fill the twelve seats with the lowest-scoring students this week, keep gradewide instruction unchanged until the next annual benchmark, and use improvement within the group as evidence that the screen correctly identified individual needs rather than an instructional deficit.
Verify administration and grade-level learning opportunity, examine core curriculum and delivery, address shared Tier 1 needs, and use multiple indicators to allocate supplemental support.
Repeat the screener until the grade produces a rate close to the district average, then discard the earlier administration as an outlier.
Rotate all below-benchmark students through the twelve seats for equal calendar time without collecting progress or implementation information.
items.rationale: When nearly half a grade is flagged, the system should investigate assessment conditions and the adequacy of universal learning opportunity before conceptualizing the pattern only as individual deficits. Conclude that the hallways are unsafe for everyone and close both routes before gathering any additional information.

items.prompt: After a schoolwide expectations campaign, office referrals decline but classroom removals rise sharply for multilingual learners during loosely structured group work. Which next step best supports prevention and equity?

Set an identical removal quota for every student group so the discipline statistics will be proportional by the next report.
Require multilingual learners to complete an additional compliance lesson before they may participate in group activities.
Examine classroom decision points with disaggregated data, observe routines, gather learner and teacher perspectives, reteach supports, and monitor revised practices.

items.prompt: A teacher finds a student’s fictional story disturbing and asks the school psychologist to declare whether the student is dangerous based only on the writing. What is the strongest response?

Address any immediate safety indicators and use a trained multidisciplinary process to gather context, behavior, communications, stressors, capabilities, and protective factors.

Administer one personality inventory and let its highest scale determine whether disciplinary removal is necessary.

Ask the school psychologist to carry out every accommodation personally because safety access is a mental-health responsibility.
Convene the safety and accessibility team to revise individualized supports, routes, communication, staff roles, rehearsal conditions, and feedback while preserving emergency readiness.

items.prompt: Following a sudden student death, staff propose a large permanent memorial and repeated assemblies with detailed accounts of the death. What guidance should the school psychologist provide?

items.prompt: A school plans attendance incentives after families report that an unreliable bus route and rotating work shifts cause many late arrivals. Which contribution from the school psychologist is most appropriate?

Refer every late student for individual counseling before discussing transportation with district operations staff.

items.prompt: A wraparound plan lists fourteen school and community activities, yet the student cannot identify what the team is trying to improve, the caregiver reports repeated appointments, and meetings review service contacts rather than daily functioning. What is the strongest next step?

items.rationale: Wraparound quality is defined by coordinated progress toward meaningful student- and family-valued outcomes, not by the number of services. items.prompt: A district family advisory process collects ranked priorities and personal testimony, but leaders finalize proposals before each meeting and record all family comments as "for awareness." items.prompt: A family returns a signed evaluation notice that was machine-translated into its home language. A community liaison explains that two translated disability terms carry stigmatizing meanings that differ from the district’s intended message. What should the school psychologist do?

items.prompt: A student tells the school psychologist that staff repeatedly mispronounce the student’s name and that the student has stopped participating in class to avoid attention. Which response best reflects culturally responsive practice?

items.prompt: A recently arrived multilingual student performs poorly on an English verbal task but demonstrates the target concept when allowed to respond with visuals, gestures, and supported home-language explanations. How should the team interpret this pattern?

items.prompt: A schoolwide prevention program shows better outcomes in schools with stronger implementation, but those schools also received more coaching and had lower staff turnover. What conclusion is most defensible?
